fail_closed_application: Before computing coarse-net economics, derive every C012 entry and exit transaction timestamp under the frozen replay semantics.
A transaction timestamp is cost-applicable only if it belongs to the frozen valid generic-support domain represented by this artifact.

If any required transaction timestamp is outside the supported domain, including a late-session exit beyond session_close_minus_60_minutes or either explicit unresolved boundary, do not impute a favorable cost and do not use the 95.3-point envelope for that unsupported context.

If any required transaction context is unsupported, classify the candidate cost confidence UNRESOLVED and the Stage-A result COST_UNRESOLVED; do not promote, do not reinterpret the boundary after seeing PnL, and do not rescue under the same identity.
If every required transaction context is supported, apply 95.3 NAS100 index points per transaction uniformly, independent of direction or realized PnL.
methodological_reason: C012 entry timing is signal-selected, so a single pre-frozen constant envelope avoids post-signal boundary selection.
Using componentwise maxima rather than a percentile creates an adverse empirical stress envelope over 27,030 valid candidate-independent DEVELOPMENT boundaries.
The fail-closed domain rule prevents the two missing refresh contexts and uncalibrated late-session exits from being silently assigned favorable costs.
The rule is intentionally coarse Discovery screening and makes no claim about Certification-grade historical fills.
